topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives and central themes concerning cancer evolution, the cell of origin, and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Drivers of Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer clones acquire competitive fitness advantages through both stepwise genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Hierarchical Models of Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stem cell properties and tissue differentiation hierarchies determine which cell types initiate tumor growth.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Promotion of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate that cancer outgrowth and maintenance depend on supportive microenvironmental signals and inflammatory stimuli rather than intrinsic cellular changes alone.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating Tumor Heterogeneity and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the experimental, single-cell sequencing, and spatial profiling technologies used to map cancer evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Synthesis of Cancer Evolution as a Multifactorial Process
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates the genetic, epigenetic, cell-of-origin, and microenvironmental factors into a unified evolutionary model of cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
